newsitem.title: SWEDEN: TENNIS-INJURED EDBERG COULD MISS REST OF DAVIS CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-INJURED EDBERG COULD MISS REST OF DAVIS CUP FINAL.

text.p: Stefan Edberg, beaten in Friday's opening singles after injuring his ankle, could be forced to sit out the the rest of the Davis Cup final.
Edberg, 30, who is bowing out of competitive tennis after the Davis Cup, lost 6-3 6-4 6-3 to France's Cedric Pioline.
A regular in Sweden's Davis Cup team for several years, Edberg fell heavily in the sixth game of the first set, twisting his ankle.
He took a three-minute time-out to have the ankle bandaged but the injury clearly troubled him for the rest of the match.
"I don't know what will happen on Sunday," a disappointed Edberg said later.
"If I am not feeling close to 100 percent it would be very hard to play. It would not be fair to me or anyone else."
Edberg, who is hoping for a fifth Davis Cup triumph to add to his six Grand Slam wins before retiring, battled bravely after his fall.
But Pioline, France's top player, took full advantage of his opponent's plight, placing shots deep and wide which Edberg struggled to reach.
Pioline, buoyed by a noisy French contingent of fans armed with scarves, drums and rattles, broke the visibly tiring Edberg twice in the third set.
He won the match after two hours 27 minutes with a lob which Edberg could not move fast enough to reach.
"I was in pain for the rest of the match after the fall," Edberg said. "I was unable to move at all like I should be able to. It was a question of hanging in there and hoping for miracles.
"Since it is the Davis Cup, and there is a lot at stake, I did what I could. But obviously I was unable to play up to my normal standards."
If Edberg is forced to pull out of Sunday's final singles against Arnaud Boetsch, one of Sweden's two doubles players, Nicklas Kulti or Jonas Bjorkman, will deputise.
"I don't know if this was my last game or not," Edberg said. "I don't even want to think about it until I wake up tomorrow. At the moment it is pretty sore."
Pioline said it was a bit upsetting to see Edberg limping but he had to remain focused on winning the match.
Swedish number one Tomas Enqvist was playing Boetsch in Friday's second singles.
